end.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 1. Equatorial Regions
end.title: The Equatorial Region: Characteristics (Soils and Vegetation)
end.coverNote: Good morning, class. Today we continue with the Equatorial Region and study its forest and its soils
end.notions: Evergreen forest, layers of the forest, hardwood, mangrove, ferrallitic soil, leaching, humus.
end.focus: Characteristics of the vegetation and soils of the Equatorial region (progression sheet, week 3).
end.competence: Learners are able to describe the equatorial forest and its soils and explain why the soils become poor when the forest is cut.
objectives: Describe the characteristics of the equatorial forest.
Name the layers of the forest and some hardwood trees.
Describe the soils of the Equatorial region.
recall: The Equatorial region is hot and wet all year.
Heavy rain falls almost every afternoon.
Plants need heat and water to grow.
end.recallNote: Check the homework on the trees and plants around Yaoundé, Douala or Bertoua.
end.justification: This lesson helps us to understand the rich forest of the Equatorial region and its fragile soils.
end.homework: List three products from the forest of southern Cameroon that are sold in the market of Garoua (for example timber, plantains or cocoa products).
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 1 (Part 3): resources and methods of exploitation.
